title: Steve Jobs at D3 (2005): iPod constraints, podcasting, Pixar's story-first process, and avoiding gatekeepers
summary: Jobs explains that great products optimize for one job and accept the second will be sub-optimal. He demos podcasting and Spotlight (built into the OS so it works better), describes how Pixar edits stories before animating, and says Apple avoids markets controlled by gatekeepers like carriers and cable companies.

principles.text: Optimize a device for one primary job; trying to do a second thing makes it sub-optimal.
principles.quote: you've got you know, games want nice big screens, music players want to fit in your pocket and you have to pick one and optimize for it and and the second thing you do will certainly be sub-optimal.

principles.text: Build features into the platform so they work better than bolt-on add-ons.
principles.quote: the reason you want to build it in the operating system because it just works better. It's far more comprehensive than an add-on tool

principles.text: Fix the story when it breaks, even when production is rolling and costs are mounting.
principles.quote: we have a story crisis on every movie and production's rolling and there's mouths to feed and something's just not working and we stop. We stop and we fix the story.

principles.text: Technology cannot rescue a weak core idea.
principles.quote: no amount of technology will turn a bad story into a good story.

principles.text: You can't keep content off the internet, so build offerings more enticing than free piracy.
principles.quote: you have to do is construct business models that are more enticing than free off the internet by some hacker.

principles.text: Edit before you make: iterate cheaply on the whole thing before committing to expensive production.
principles.quote: we have to edit our film before we make it, not after.
